technical_and_design_decisions: Implement examples using the existing Spring XD samples repository conventions and supported Spring XD module APIs rather than introducing a new application framework.

Use Kafka as the message bus for both streaming demonstrations, with separate reusable business-logic components for real-time and batch/reprocessing paths to illustrate lambda architecture and avoid duplicated logic.
Represent Kafka demonstrations as runnable sample stream and batch definitions, including log aggregation, analysis, reliable replay, and decoupled processing stages.
Implement Sqoop demonstrations as batch samples covering JDBC-to-HDFS and HDFS-to-JDBC movement, using configurable JDBC connection, table, directory, and Sqoop options.
Treat the JDBC-to-HDFS requirement as a separately documented example even where it shares implementation concepts with the Sqoop sample.
Update documentation generation and publishing scripts to remove obsolete generated-document tasks and link rewriting while preserving the repository's remaining documentation workflow.

Document Storm and Spark Streaming comparisons by mapping representative Spring XD samples to equivalent implementation concepts, rather than porting or rewriting the underlying Storm or Spark runtimes.
Port the Smart Grid demonstration into the repository using existing sample structure, configuration conventions, and available Spring XD stream and batch primitives.
Add the file-sink nameExpression option as an alternative to the existing naming behavior, mapping it to the complete filename-generator-expression value while retaining backward compatibility.

Use automated unit, configuration, and sample-level integration checks where practical, with external-system tests isolated behind configurable Kafka, Hadoop, HDFS, JDBC, Storm, and Spark dependencies.
assumptions: The existing Spring XD samples repository, build, documentation conventions, and relevant module APIs are available and buildable without a broad framework migration.
Kafka, Sqoop, Hadoop/HDFS, JDBC database, Storm, and Spark test environments or representative fixtures are available; provisioning production-grade clusters is out of scope.
The source code and configuration for the Smart Grid demo from s1-2014 are available and legally usable for porting.
The increment requires examples, documentation, build changes, and the file-sink option, but does not require production deployment, operational runbooks, or performance benchmarking.
The existing file sink already supports filename-generator-expression internally, so the requested change primarily exposes and validates an alternative nameExpression option.
Compatibility with existing stream definitions and existing file naming behavior is required.
A workday represents one developer day of implementation, review preparation, testing, and documentation effort; elapsed time for external environment availability is excluded.
No additional contributor coordination or parallel development is assumed because one developer performs all work.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing samples, build scripts, documentation layout, stream and batch conventions, file sink implementation, and relevant historical examples; define the implementation structure and acceptance checks for all user stories.
Implement the Kafka-based log ingestion, aggregation, and analysis pipeline, including stream definitions, processing components, configuration, sample data, and runnable usage instructions.

activities.activity_name: Kafka lambda architecture and replay sample
activities.activity_description: Implement the real-time and batch/reprocessing paths demonstrating shared business logic, reduced coupling between stages, and reliable Kafka-driven reprocessing without duplicating domain behavior.
Validate Kafka stream definitions and processing behavior with representative events, document setup and execution, and correct configuration or integration issues found during testing.
Create the Sqoop batch sample for importing relational data into HDFS, including job configuration, parameterization, sample input schema, execution instructions, and expected output.
Create the reverse Sqoop batch sample for exporting HDFS data into a relational database, including destination setup, configurable options, execution instructions, and expected results.

activities.activity_name: Sqoop sample testing and integration fixes
activities.activity_description: Run the Sqoop examples against representative JDBC and HDFS environments, verify data movement in both directions, and resolve compatibility, schema, parameter, or documentation issues.

Implement and document the separately requested JDBC-to-HDFS data-movement example, reusing appropriate repository components while making its purpose, configuration, and execution independently understandable.
Modify the Gradle documentation-generation workflow, remove pushGeneratedDocs and related obsolete tasks, eliminate no-longer-needed link rewriting, and verify the resulting documentation build.

Produce a field-engineer-oriented comparison of the relevant Storm examples and Spring XD implementations, covering topology concepts, processing stages, configuration, deployment, and implementation mapping.
Produce a corresponding comparison of Spark Streaming examples and Spring XD implementations, explaining equivalent data-flow, processing, configuration, execution, and operational concepts.
Port the s1-2014 Smart Grid demonstration into the samples repository, adapt configuration and APIs to the target repository conventions, add required resources, and document how to run it.

Add the alternative nameExpression option for file-sink stream definitions, map it to complete filename-generator-expression control, preserve existing naming behavior, and update command/configuration parsing and validation.

activities.activity_name: File sink feature tests and documentation
activities.activity_description: Add unit and integration coverage for default naming, custom nameExpression values, edge cases, and backward compatibility; update user-facing examples and option documentation.

activities.activity_name: Cross-increment build, regression, and packaging verification
activities.activity_description: Run the complete build and relevant sample checks, verify documentation generation and repository packaging, perform regression testing for existing examples and file sinks, and fix integration issues.

activities.activity_name: Final code review preparation and delivery cleanup
activities.activity_description: Review changed files for consistency and maintainability, normalize sample configuration and documentation, remove temporary artifacts, and prepare the completed increment for submission.
